bottom_line: In CHARM-Added, candesartan vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF (unadjusted hazard ratio 0.85 [95% CI 0.75–0.96]).
implications: These data support that adding candesartan to background ACE-inhibitor therapy reduced time-to-first cardiovascular death or CHF hospital admission versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.85 [95% CI 0.75–0.96]) over a median 41 months. The trial also reports higher permanent discontinuation due to adverse events/laboratory abnormalities with candesartan (24.2 vs 18.3), including more hyperkalaemia- and creatinine-related discontinuations; the results do not establish an all-cause mortality reduction (unadjusted 0.89 [0.77–1.02]).

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind comparison of candesartan (target 32 mg once daily) versus placebo added to ACE inhibitor therapy in CHF with reduced LVEF.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned patients, in a double-blind way, candesartan or matching placebo

major_points.text: Population: NYHA class II–IV CHF, LVEF ≤40%, on ACE inhibitor at constant dose for ≥30 days; 2548 patients enrolled.
major_points.quote: enrolled 2548 patients with New York Heart Association functional class II–IV CHF and left-ventricular ejection fraction 40% or lower, and who were being treated with ACE inhibitors.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was cardiovascular death or unplanned admission to hospital for worsening CHF; analysis by intention to treat.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was cardiovascular death or unplanned admission to hospital for the management of worsening CHF.
The median duration of follow up was 41 months.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred in 483/1276 vs 538/1272; hazard ratio 0.85 (95% CI 0.75–0.96).
major_points.quote: 483 (38%) patients in the candesartan group and 538 (42%) in the placebo group experienced the primary outcome (unadjusted hazard ratio 0·85 [95% CI 0·75–0·96], p=0·011

major_points.text: Cardiovascular death was lower with candesartan: 302 (23.7%) vs 347 (27.3%), unadjusted hazard ratio 0.84 (0.72–0.98).
major_points.quote: There were 302 (24%) cardiovascular deaths in the candesartan group compared with 347 (27%) in the placebo group (unadjusted 0·84 [0·72–0·98], p=0·029

major_points.text: CHF hospital admission was reduced: 309 (24.2%) vs 356 (28.0%), unadjusted hazard ratio 0.83 (0.71–0.96).
Hyperkalaemia-related discontinuation was higher with candesartan: 44 (3.4) vs 9 (0.7).
Increase in creatinine-related discontinuation was higher with candesartan: 100 (7.8) vs 52 (4.1).
